answer: Unique-Output Quota Registry. Each identity must submit a fresh, verifiable artifact (a compiled program, a signed sonnet) whose hash is checked against a global registry; duplicates are rejected outright. Attackers cannot clone identities because every clone needs novel, costly-to-produce work. Like a glacier, the registry advances slowly but irreversibly, and a whisper of reuse disqualifies the submission. Per-identity cost is the compute or authorship to generate one unique artifact, paid again for every fake identity.
